statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-32202 is a protection mechanism failure in Windows Shell, a component of the Windows operating system, that allows network spoofing (https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-32202). It is not a .NET vulnerability: Microsoft has published no .NET advisory for it, and the .NET 10.0.6 release notes do not list it (https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.6/10.0.6.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. They hold the .NET runtime, ASP.NET Core and SDK built for Linux on musl, and none of them contains Windows Shell or any native Windows PE file; every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly.

CVE-2026-32202 is a protection mechanism failure in Windows Shell that allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network. Microsoft and NVD list only Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server releases as affected; it is not a .NET vulnerability (https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-32202, https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-32202). It matches this owner only because Alpine's dotnet8-runtime package lists CVE-2026-32202 among the fixes for 8.0.26-r0 (https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/community/dotnet8-runtime/APKBUILD), while Microsoft's .NET 8.0.26 release notes list CVE-2026-32203, a System.Security.Cryptography.Xml denial of service, alongside the other fixes in that release and do not mention CVE-2026-32202 (https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.26/8.0.26.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: none of them contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file; every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly with a CLR header, every loadable ELF program and shared library in them links against musl libc, and the static .a archives they hold are .NET host, runtime and native-library archives built for Alpine. Windows Shell is a Windows operating system component and is not part of these packages.

CVE-2026-32202 is a protection mechanism failure in Windows Shell, a component of the Windows operating system, that allows network spoofing (https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-32202, https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-32202). It is not a .NET vulnerability: Microsoft has no .NET advisory for it, and the .NET 9.0.15 release notes do not list it (https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.15/9.0.15.md), although Alpine's dotnet9-runtime 9.0.15-r0 security fixes list it. DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: they hold the .NET runtime, ASP.NET Core and SDK for Linux, none of them contains Windows Shell or any native Windows PE file, and every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly.
